correctness.rationale: For every real epsilon strictly between zero and one and every fixed positive integer trial count, the actual two-matrix joint diagonalization loss is derived from the exact spectral projectors of the Gaussian weighted sum. Its squared off-diagonal objective is exactly twice epsilon squared times (g1 squared plus g2 squared) divided by (g1 squared plus epsilon squared times g2 squared). Uniform Gaussian angle and independence establish the finite-parameter survival function. Exact integration establishes one-trial expected squared loss of twice epsilon, as well as the first-moment elliptic integral. For two trials, tail integration has an integrand asymptotic to 8 divided by pi squared and z over a logarithmically widening central interval, with the endpoint contributions negligible on the logarithmic scale. For three or more trials, a power-integrable envelope justifies dominated convergence; the three-trial constant is 24 log(2) divided by pi squared. Catalan's definite integral gives the two-trial first-moment coefficient. Direct rotation proves that the deterministic optimum squared loss is twice epsilon squared. The embedded verifier independently corroborates exact rational matrix identities, angles, CDF values, and representative integrals. No finite experiment substitutes for the proof.

originality.rationale: The 2022 He-Kressner RJD paper supplies the algorithm, loss and general high-probability inverse-amplification bounds; it observes faster failure-tail decrease under restarts. The present exact 2x2 noncommuting family supplies finite-noise equality in law, sharp attained lower bounds and the minimal trial budget for optimal-order expected squared loss, including explicit logarithmic/Catalan constants. Primary full text and two adjacent full-text sources were compared; neither includes the exact law or implication. Absence from sampled searchable records is not proof of novelty. value.rationale: The motivating randomized diagonalization paper offers high-probability perturbation guarantees and empirically observes improved failure tails under independent trials, raising the natural question whether the approximation has optimal-order expected squared loss at a fixed restart budget. This exact two-by-two noncommuting benchmark proves a substantive three-way distinction: one trial incurs expected squared loss of order epsilon, two incur epsilon squared times log(1/epsilon), and three achieve order epsilon squared, matching the deterministic optimum up to a finite constant. The finite-noise survival function and explicit elliptic, Catalan and log(2) coefficients give reproducible quantitative benchmarks for robust restart policies. The result is confined to this family and does not claim a general runtime or convergence theorem.
